land.text: Pajang, whose last ruler submitted to Sutawijaya in 1586 (Mataram page: 'This event in 1586, marked the end of Pajang kingdom and the rise of its former vassal, the Mataram Sultanate')

predecessors.note: Mataram's own core (Kota Gede) came first, from the 1584 independence; the Pajang lands followed in 1586. Cliopatria's Pajang shape of 1582 and its Mataram shape of 1588 are the same polygon.

land.text: the Surakarta half of the Giyanti partition (Pakubuwono II's court at Surakarta from 1745/1746)

successors.note: The Mataram page: 'The kingdom of Mataram was divided in 1755 under an agreement signed in Giyanti'. Cliopatria's Surakarta row starts in 1744, eleven years early.

land.text: the Yogyakarta half of the Giyanti partition, the Sultanate of Mangkubumi

successors.note: Mangkubumi 'raise[d] his followers into rebellion in May 1746'; the Yogyakarta Sultanate dates from Giyanti (1755). Cliopatria's row starts in 1744.

land.text: the north coast (pasisir), East Java and Madura, which the VOC held by 1743: 'by 1743 Mataram only consists of areas around Surakarta, Yogyakarta, Kedu and Bagelen'

successors.note: Land that left Mataram before the end, in 1742-1743, not at 1755.

capitals.name: Kota Gede
capitals.note: Infobox 'Kota Gede (1587-1613)'; the dossier starts in 1584 and no earlier seat is on the page. Coordinates are the modern district of Kotagede (Yogyakarta).

capitals.name: Karta (Kerta)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Karta (1613-1645)'; approximate position, next to Pleret.

capitals.name: Plered (Pleret)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Plered (1646-1680)'. Rebels took the court in June 1677; Pangeran Puger held it 1677-1680 and August-November 1681.

capitals.name: Kartasura
capitals.note: Infobox 'Kartosuro (1680-1745)'; 'Amangkurat II built a new capital at Kartasura' in 1680 (Trunajaya page). The rebels captured it on 30 June 1742.

capitals.name: Surakarta (Solo)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Surakarta (1745-1755)'; the text says Pakubuwana II 'moved there in 1746'.

correction.text: the Mataram lands round Kota Gede before Pajang fell, a 35 km circle at the site of the capital

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1588 but the infobox gives 'Independence from Pajang Sultanate: 1584'. The page names no boundary for these two years; the circle is a reading.

correction.text: the Mataram core with Pajang's Central Java lands: the same reading the kingdom-of-pajana dossier gives for the Pajang polygon

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'This event in 1586, marked the end of Pajang kingdom and the rise of its former vassal, the Mataram Sultanate.' Cliopatria's 1588 outline adds a strip of western East Java (Madiun and Kediri) beyond Central Java and Yogyakarta, which no opened page dates before 1615; the ledger adds it in 1588 at confidence 1.

45.3 k km2 for 1588-1618: Central Java, Yogyakarta and a strip of western East Java (Madiun, Kediri). The pages put the first conquests in East Java in 1615 (Wirasaba), so the Madiun-Kediri strip is unverified: the Sultan Agung page has Surabaya and Malang resisting in 1614. The infobox gives no area; Java with Madura is about 133 k km2 against Cliopatria's 65.7 k km2 maximum (ratio 0.5), the other half being West Java (Banten, Batavia, Cirebon, Priangan) and Blambangan.

57.7 k km2 for 1619-1621: the outline now holds Wirasaba and Mojokerto (1615), Pasuruan (1617) and Tuban (1619) and not yet Madura or Surabaya; this fits 'Wirasaba (present-day Mojoagung, near Mojokerto)', 'Pasuruan... was taken in 1617' and 'Tuban... was taken in 1619'. Lasem (1616) was already inside the 1588 outline.

correction.text: the 1619 outline for 1622-1623: Cliopatria's 1622 step adds Madura (taken in 1624) and part of Surabaya (1625), two years and three years early

keyframe_review.note: Verdict changes the years: 'captured the island of Madura, another ally of Surabaya, in 1624' and 'Agung finally conquered Surabaya in a siege in 1625'. The ledger gains of 1624 and 1625 add them; the 1626 outline holds both.

65.7 k km2, the maximum: 'By 1625, Mataram was the undisputed ruler of most of Java', with Madura and Surabaya in. The outline stops short of West Java, Blambangan and the Borneo and Sumatran vassals ('vassals in Palembang, Sukadana, and Jambi', Mataram page), which are tints in the ledger or other states' land. Holds 1625-1676 (Surabaya fell in 1625).

correction.text: the realm as before the rebellion, which the ledger shortens: rebel-held coast, Plered and Kediri come out and return as the page dates them

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Mataram shape for 1677-1682, but Amangkurat II reigned throughout ('In 1680, Amangkurat II ascended as the king of Mataram by receiving his crown from the Dutch') and the VOC and Mataram together crushed the rebels.

correction.text: the 1626 outline: Cliopatria's 1683 outline drops the whole Central Java north coast from Brebes to Rembang (43 cells), but the pages cede only Semarang (1705) and pledge the harbour towns' income

keyframe_review.note: 54.6 k km2 against 65.7 k. The Trunajaya page has the VOC promised the income of the northern harbour towns and the Priangan highlands and Semarang to be 'ceded' (September 1677); the Mataram page has the VOC 'given Semarang' in 1705 and Pakubuwono II offering 'absolute control over all northern coasts of Java' only in March 1742, which implies the coast was still Mataram's in between. The pledge of revenue is not a loss of land; the cession of Semarang is dated 1705.

correction.text: the 1626 outline without Semarang and without eastern Madura: 'In 1705 he agreed to cede the regions of Cirebon and eastern part of Madura' and 'The VOC was given Semarang as new headquarters'

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1706 outline is the 1683 one, with no change for the 1705 cessions. The cession of 'the regions of Cirebon' touches land outside every Mataram outline (Cirebon is not in it); the ledger records it as a loss.

correction.text: the 1706 outline, holding 1741-1742; from 1743 the new keyframe mataram-sultanate_1743 takes over

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws 54.6 k km2 for 1741-1743, but the page says 'by 1743 Mataram only consists of areas around Surakarta, Yogyakarta, Kedu and Bagelen' (the coast and East Java lost in the Chinese war of 1740-1743); this verdict holds for 1741-1742 only.

correction.text: 'areas around Surakarta, Yogyakarta, Kedu and Bagelen': the Yogyakarta province, 50 km round Surakarta, 60 km round Magelang for Kedu and a 35 km circle at Purworejo for Bagelen

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the interior of Central Java, about 19 k km2 against Cliopatria's 54.6 k, to the Giyanti partition of 1755. Cliopatria's Surakarta Sunanate and Sultan of Yogyakarta rows (3.7 k and 4.2 k km2) start in 1744 inside this land, and its Dutch Republic row covers most of the lost coast from 1744. Kedu and Bagelen are not gazetteer names, so circles stand in.

region.text: the Mataram lands round Kota Gede

ledger.note: 1584: Sutawijaya (Panembahan Senapati) makes Mataram independent of Pajang. Infobox 'Independence from Pajang Sultanate: 1584'; 'Sutawijaya replaced his father around 1584'. The page gives no boundary, only the capital Kota Gede.

1586: Pajang ends and Mataram takes its lands. 'This event in 1586, marked the end of Pajang kingdom and the rise of its former vassal, the Mataram Sultanate.' The page names no land; the reading is the kingdom-of-pajana dossier's.

region.text: the strip of western East Java in Cliopatria's 1588 outline (Madiun and Kediri)

ledger.note: 1588: Cliopatria's first Mataram outline holds Madiun and Kediri. None of the pages opened dates or even mentions this conquest; the Sultan Agung page has Wirasaba as the first East Java conquest in 1615. A gap-filler should look at Senapati's reign (1584-1601).
1613: the court moves from Kota Gede to Karta as Sultan Agung takes the throne (infobox 'Karta (1613-1645)'; 'Sultan Agung became the ruler of Mataram in 1613').

1615: Agung takes Wirasaba, the first East Java conquest. 'used this in 1615, to conquer Wirasaba (present-day Mojoagung, near Mojokerto)', after failing against Surabaya and Malang in 1614; the Mataram page has him repel allied Surabaya forces there.

region.text: Lasem, near Rembang on the north coast

ledger.note: 1616: Lasem falls. 'Lasem was conquered later in 1616' (the Mataram page: 'The coastal city of Lasem, near Rembang, was conquered in 1616'). Cliopatria's 1588 outline already includes it.
1617: Pasuruan is taken. 'Pasuruan was taken in 1617' (Mataram page: 'Pasuruan, southeast of Surabaya, was taken in 1617').

region.text: Tuban, one of the oldest and largest port cities on the coast of Java

ledger.note: 1619: Tuban falls. 'Tuban was taken in 1619'.

region.text: Sukadana in southwest Kalimantan, Surabaya's ally

ledger.note: 1622: Mataram captures Sukadana, which the page then lists among its vassals. 'capturing Sukadana, Surabaya's ally in southwest Kalimantan in 1622'; 'with vassals in Palembang, Sukadana, and Jambi'. The Tanjungpura page says only that 'Adipati Kendal with his Mataram Expedition, attacked Matan (1622)' and records no vassalage.
1624: Madura is taken after a fierce battle. 'captured the island of Madura, another ally of Surabaya, in 1624'.
1625: Surabaya falls after five years of war. 'Agung finally conquered Surabaya in a siege in 1625'; 'By 1625, Mataram was the undisputed ruler of most of Java.'

c. 1625: Cirebon in Mataram's sphere. The page says only 'Agung himself took the hand of Cirebon Princess as his consort' (no year) and that Cirebon 'was forced to shift allegiance from Mataram to the Dutch' under Amangkurat II; 1625 is the page's year for Mataram ruling 'most of Java', a bridge.

region.text: the Priangan highlands, where Sumedang and Ukur rose in 1631-1636

ledger.note: 1631: Mataram's hold on the Priangan is first shown by its suppression of rebellions: the page says Sumedang and Ukur were suppressed in 1631-1636. The page does not say when they became Mataram's; the year is a bridge.

1639: Blambangan surrenders. 'Blambangan surrendered in 1639, but quickly regained their independence in 1659.' The blambangan-kingdom dossier carries the 1635-1639 contest; Gelgel (Bali) had backed Blambangan as a buffer.
1641: the ruler takes the Sultan's title. 'In 1641, Sunan Agung had an Arabic title, Sultan Abdullah Muhammad Maulana of Mataram, bestowed by imams in Mecca.' Same state: colour continues.
1645: Sultan Agung dies (spring 1645) and, with him, the greatest extent. No page opened records when Sukadana left Mataram's orbit; the year is a bridge.
1646: the court moves to Plered (infobox 'Plered (1646-1680)') under Amangkurat I; 'Agung died in the spring of 1645.'

1659: Blambangan regains its independence. 'Blambangan surrendered in 1639, but quickly regained their independence in 1659' (the page adds that it rejoined Bali in 1697; the blambangan-kingdom dossier dates the break from Mataram to 1665).

region.text: Madura and the northern coastal towns from Surabaya to Cirebon, Jepara excepted

ledger.note: 1676: Trunajaya's rebels take the north coast. the Trunajaya page has rebels take most northern coastal towns, from Surabaya to Cirebon, except Jepara (1676-1677), after the victory at Gegodog in September 1676. (Reviewer se-02-g, 2026-10-19: Madura added: the Trunajaya page has Trunajaya 'the master of Madura' from 1671 and the rebel army crossing 'from Madura to Java' in September 1676; the trunajaya-rebellion dossier founds the rebel state on Madura in 1676 and ledger 20 here regains Madura in 1677.)

region.text: Kediri, where the royal treasury was taken

ledger.note: 1677: Kediri becomes the rebel base. The page dates only the treasury's move there (June 1677) and the town's fall (25 November 1678).

region.text: Madura and the north-coast towns other than Surabaya

ledger.note: 1677: Madura and the rest of the rebel coast return to Mataram and the VOC. The Trunajaya page has, after the April 1677 Surabaya campaign, 'VOC forces also took Madura, Trunajaya's native island, and laid his residence there in ruin', and Amangkurat II accepting the VOC's terms at Jepara in September 1677; it does not name the other coast towns' return. This mirrors the trunajaya-rebellion dossier's 1677 loss. (Reviewer se-02-g, 2026-10-19: confidence raised from 1 to 2 on that sentence.)
April 1677: Surabaya is retaken. 'In April 1677 the fleet sailed to Surabaya, where Trunajaya was based'; Trunajaya fled and Surabaya fell to VOC and Mataram forces.

June 1677: the rebels take Plered. The king, ill, fled west (he died at Tegal in July) and the royal treasury went with the rebels to Kediri; Mataram page: they 'captured the king's court at Plered in Mataram in mid-1677'.

September 1677: Amangkurat II, on VOC ships at Jepara, agrees to concessions. 'The Priangan highlands and Semarang would be ceded to the VOC' and the VOC was promised the income of the northern harbour towns (Mataram page: 'Mataram has to hand over Bogor, Karawang and Priangan to the VOC', tied to 1680). Semarang is dated 1705 below.
25 November 1678: Kediri falls to VOC and Mataram forces under François Tack; the court of Amangkurat II is then set up at Surabaya. the page has Kediri fall on 25 November 1678.

region.text: Plered, from which the VOC and royal forces drove Puger

ledger.note: 1680: Plered is recovered. the Trunajaya page has, for September-November 1680, Amangkurat II building a new capital at Kartasura while the VOC and royal forces drove Puger out of Plered. Puger had held it since 1677-1678.
1680: the court moves to the new capital Kartasura (infobox 'Kartosuro (1680-1745)').

c. 1680: Cirebon leaves Mataram. The Mataram page, in Amangkurat II's reign, has 'Cirebon too was forced to shift allegiance from Mataram to the Dutch'; the Trunajaya page has Cirebon declaring independence with Banten's support in 1677-1678. The page gives no year for the shift.
August 1681: Puger retakes Plered. the Trunajaya page has, for August-November 1681, Puger retaking Plered and then being defeated in November and pardoned by his brother.
November 1681: Puger is defeated and pardoned by Amangkurat II, and Plered returns.

1705: the VOC receives Semarang. 'The VOC was given Semarang as new headquarters' under Pakubuwono I; Amangkurat II had 'promised to give the VOC the port town of Semarang if they lend him some troops' (c. 1677-1680).
1705: eastern Madura goes to the VOC. 'In 1705 he agreed to cede the regions of Cirebon and eastern part of Madura.'

region.text: the regions of Cirebon, where Mataram kept only nominal rights

ledger.note: 1705: Mataram cedes its rights in Cirebon. The same sentence names 'the regions of Cirebon'; Cirebon is outside every Mataram outline and had left Mataram's orbit by c. 1680.

region.text: the north coast, East Java and Madura, the land outside 'the areas around Surakarta, Yogyakarta, Kedu and Bagelen'

ledger.note: By 1743: the Chinese war leaves Mataram a Central Java interior. In March 1742 Pakubuwono II offered the VOC 'absolute control over all northern coasts of Java'; the rebels took Kartasura on 30 June 1742; 'by 1743 Mataram only consists of areas around Surakarta, Yogyakarta, Kedu and Bagelen.' The page dates no treaty; Pakubuwono II's own page (1726-1742, 1743-1749) is silent on it.

1745: the court moves from Kartasura to Surakarta (infobox 'Surakarta (1745-1755)'; the text says Pakubuwana II 'built a new kraton in Surakarta or Solo and moved there in 1746', and Pakubuwono II's page gives no date).

region.text: the interior of Central Java, divided at Giyanti

ledger.note: 1755: Mataram is partitioned at Giyanti. 'The kingdom of Mataram was divided in 1755 under an agreement signed in Giyanti'; 'The treaty divided nominal control over central Java between the Yogyakarta Sultanate' and the Surakarta Sunanate. The Third War of Succession had begun with Mangkubumi's rebellion in May 1746.

wars.name: Mataram conquest of the Surabaya league
belligerents: Surabaya and its allies (Wirasaba, Pasuruan, Tuban, Madura)
wars.outcome: Agung attacked Surabaya and Malang in 1614 and failed, then took Wirasaba (1615), Lasem (1616), Pasuruan (1617), Tuban (1619), Madura (1624) and, after five years of war, Surabaya (1625).
wars.note: The Mataram page dates the five years of siege warfare as ending in 1625, so the war on Surabaya itself ran c. 1620-1625.

wars.name: Mataram expedition to Sukadana
wars.outcome: Mataram captured Sukadana, Surabaya's ally in southwest Kalimantan, in 1622 (Mataram page); the Tanjungpura page has Adipati Kendal's expedition attack Matan that year.
wars.note: Recorded as a vassalage from 1622 at confidence 2.

wars.name: Sieges of Batavia
wars.outcome: Agung's attempt to capture Batavia in 1628-1629 failed; no land changed hands.
wars.note: The page gives one campaign, not two sieges; after it Agung turned on the Balinese backing Blambangan (page: he succeeded in Java but could not extend his power to Bali).

wars.name: Suppression of Tembayat, Sumedang and Ukur

zones.text: Sumedang and Ukur in the Priangan highlands

wars.outcome: Tembayat was crushed in 1630 and Sumedang and Ukur were suppressed in 1631-1636 (the page's wording).
wars.note: The page gives no territorial change.

wars.name: Mataram conquest of Blambangan
wars.outcome: Blambangan surrendered in 1639 and regained its independence in 1659.
wars.note: The blambangan-kingdom dossier carries the contest from 1635; no page opened here dates the start of the campaign.

wars.name: Trunajaya rebellion

zones.text: the north coast from Surabaya to Cirebon

wars.outcome: The VOC and Mataram crushed the rebels (Kediri 25 November 1678, Trunajaya's surrender 26 December 1679); Amangkurat II received the VOC's price in the September 1677 concessions and moved to Kartasura in 1680; Puger was pardoned in November 1681.

wars.name: First Javanese War of Succession
wars.outcome: it 'dragged on for five years before the Dutch managed to install Pakubuwana' I (Mataram page); in 1705 Mataram agreed to cede Cirebon and eastern Madura and the VOC was given Semarang.
wars.note: The Mataram page dates the war 1704-1708 (the Javanese Wars of Succession page: 1703-1708) and names no territory in it; the cessions are in the ledger.

wars.name: Second Javanese War of Succession
wars.outcome: The page gives only the dates (the Mataram page: 1719-1723) and no territorial result. The Mataram page records, under the preceding reign, interior East Java regencies (Ponorogo, Madiun, Magetan, Jogorogo) joining a rebellion and 'The VOC managed to capture Surabaya after a bloody war in 1718'.
wars.note: Surabaya's 1718 recapture by the VOC is not recorded as a change of ruler.

wars.name: Chinese War (Java War of 1740-1743)
wars.outcome: The rebels took Kartasura on 30 June 1742; the northern coast was cleared of rebels by October 1742 with the VOC; 'by 1743 Mataram only consists of areas around Surakarta, Yogyakarta, Kedu and Bagelen'.
wars.note: 'On 7 October 1740, several Chinese mobs attacked Europeans outside the city' began it; Bekasi (June 1741) and Juwana (May 1741) fell to the Chinese; Cakraningrat IV 'had controlled the stretch of east coast from Tuban to Sedayu' (late November 1741); the Dutch ousted him from Madura in 1745.

wars.name: Third Javanese War of Succession
wars.outcome: Mangkubumi rose in May 1746 (the page dates the war 1749-1755); it ended with the Giyanti agreement of 1755, which divided Mataram between the Surakarta Sunanate and the Yogyakarta Sultanate.
wars.note: The Mataram page also has the Third War beginning with Mangkubumi's 1746 rebellion; the Javanese Wars of Succession page says 'Mataram was carved into three weak Vorstenlanden' (a third later), 'independent in name only'.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary: Java's interior and coast are drawn from Cliopatria's outlines and circles round named towns. The only frontier fixed by an instrument is the Giyanti partition of 1755, which this dossier does not draw.

sources.title: Mataram Sultanate
sources.note: Identity, infobox, capitals, conquests 1615-1625, Batavia, Trunajaya, Dutch cessions 1705, Chinese war, Giyanti. Read twice with different questions.

sources.title: Sultan Agung of Mataram
sources.note: Dated conquests 1613-1625, Batavia 1628-1629, rebellions 1630-1636, the Sultan title 1641, death 1645.

sources.title: Trunajaya rebellion
sources.note: Rebel-held towns 1676-1678, Plered 1677, September 1677 concessions, Kediri, Puger, Kartasura 1680.

sources.title: Javanese Wars of Succession
sources.note: Thin: gives the war dates (1703-1708, 1719-1722, 1749-1755) and says Mataram was carved into three Vorstenlanden; no cessions, no 1743 treaty, no Giyanti terms.

sources.title: Pakubuwono II
sources.note: Thin: reigns 1726-1742 and 1743-1749, death 20 December 1749; no 1742-1749 events or treaty.

notes: Five pages were opened (the budget). Cliopatria's Mataram row has a gap 1677-1682 (the Trunajaya rebellion), which a new keyframe fills; it also starts four years after the page's 1584 independence (new keyframes for 1584-1587) and ends in 1743 although the page ends the state in 1755 (a new keyframe for 1743-1754). Its 1683 shape drops the Central Java north coast, which the pages do not support (the VOC was pledged the harbour towns' income and given Semarang in 1705; the coast was offered whole to the VOC only in March 1742), so the shape is restored to the 1626 outline; the 1706 and 1741 shapes repeat the 1683 one without the 1705 cessions and are corrected. The 1743 interior rests on one sentence ('areas around Surakarta, Yogyakarta, Kedu and Bagelen') and circles; Kedu and Bagelen, Madura, Priangan, Lasem, Jepara and Kartasura are not in the gazetteer. The page dates no 1743 treaty and the two pages meant to supply it (Javanese Wars of Succession, Pakubuwono II) were thin. Cliopatria's Surakarta Sunanate and Sultan of Yogyakarta rows begin in 1744, eleven years before Giyanti and inside this dossier's land; those dossiers should start them at 1745/1755. Vassals not recorded for want of a date: Palembang and Jambi ('vassals in Palembang, Sukadana, and Jambi', no years); Sukadana's start is the page's 1622 but its end is a confidence-1 bridge; the Priangan and Cirebon relations are confidence 1 at the start. Trunajaya's rebel state has its own dossier (trunajaya-rebellion). The lord of Giri (beaten April 1680) and Pangeran Puger are counterparts without dossiers. The Dutch (VOC) are counterpart 'dutch-republic', the Cliopatria row that holds the company's land.
